relevance_rank_note: A direct APOE4-versus-APOE3 binding comparison at the LDL receptor using native lipoproteins from E4/4 and E3/3 homozygous human donors competing against 125I-LDL on human hepatoma and human fibroblast cells, so B1 (adhesion to a recycling receptor) is measured itself; it measures no receptor recycling and uses no brain cells.

description: VLDL isolated from APOE4/4 homozygous men competed against 125I-LDL for the LDL receptor on Hep G2 cells more effectively than paired APOE3/3 VLDL, the paired E4/4-to-E3/3 IC50 ratio being significantly below unity, so E4/4 VLDL bound the LDL receptor more tightly. Effect detail: the same Hep G2 VLDL experiment reported unpaired gives IC50 3.7+/-1.3 (E4/4) vs 6.1+/-3.7 ug apoB/ml (E3/3), P<0.08 (not significant); the paired ratio test and the unpaired comparison are one experiment and are recorded here as one finding. The P recorded is the unpaired E4/4-versus-E3/3 comparison of the IC50 values themselves (3.7 +/- 1.3 vs 6.1 +/- 3.7 ug apoB/ml, P < 0.08), which the authors call marginally lower; the separate P < 0.05 in this table is a one-sample test of the paired ratio against unity, not a two-group test.
quote: In Hep G2 cells, E4/4 VLDL was more effective than E3/3 VLDL in competing for the LDL receptor, the IC50 ratio being significantly lower than unity (0.73 ± 0.31, P< 0.05).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower IC50 against the LDL receptor, i.e. tighter VLDL binding)
system: Hep G2 human hepatoma cell monolayers grown to 75% confluence and preincubated 24-48 h in lipoprotein-deficient serum to upregulate LDL receptors, then incubated 2 h at 4 C and pH 7.4 with 10 ug apoB/ml 125I-LDL from the paired E3/3 donor plus a concentration range of unlabelled native VLDL isolated by flotation ultracentrifugation from fasting plasma of APOE4/4 or paired APOE3/3 Caucasian male donors aged 42 +/- 6 and 45 +/- 7 years not on lipid-lowering therapy; competition IC50 in ug apoB/ml by four-parameter logistic fit, paired E4/4-to-E3/3 IC50 ratio tested against unity by two-tailed t-test.
human_check: Corrected 2026-11-23 (team leader approved) after a blind referee check: the row previously carried P < 0.05, which the source attaches to the paired IC50 ratio tested AGAINST UNITY, not to the APOE4-versus-APOE3 group comparison (P < 0.08). Against flag follows the printed P under the non-significant-trend convention in decisions.md. The direction still FAVOURS H4 (E4/4 VLDL competes more effectively) and the authors' own one-tailed reading gives P < 0.05, so a reviewer may prefer to read this as weak support rather than against. No figure image was viewed; values are from printed Table 2 and the Results text. n = 7 pairs in the Hep G2 columns (Methods say eight; subject pair 6 has values only in the fibroblast columns), independently counted by the referee.

description: In the same competition assay run on human skin fibroblasts, VLDL from APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 donors competed equally against 125I-LDL for the LDL receptor, the paired IC50 ratio sitting at unity, so no isoform difference in binding was detected in this cell type. Effect detail: the same Hep G2 VLDL experiment reported unpaired gives IC50 3.7+/-1.3 (E4/4) vs 6.1+/-3.7 ug apoB/ml (E3/3), P<0.08 (not significant); the paired ratio test and the unpaired comparison are one experiment and are recorded here as one finding.
quote: In contrast to results on Hep G2 cells, the data do not support a difference in the affinity of E4/4 and E3/3 VLDL for the LDL receptors on fibroblasts.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in VLDL competition IC50 at the fibroblast LDL receptor)
system: Monolayer cultures of foreskin fibroblasts from a healthy male donor, grown to 75% confluence and preincubated 24-48 h in lipoprotein-deficient serum to upregulate LDL receptors, then incubated 2 h at 4 C and pH 7.4 with 10 ug apoB/ml 125I-LDL from the paired E3/3 donor plus a concentration range of native VLDL from APOE4/4 or paired APOE3/3 male donors aged 42 +/- 6 and 45 +/- 7 years; competition IC50 in ug apoB/ml, paired E4/4-to-E3/3 ratio.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Against: true, a null. The paired fibroblast IC50 ratio is 0.94 +/- 0.49 with no P printed for it: Table 2's dagger footnote (P < 0.05 vs unity) is attached to the Hep G2 ratio only, and the asterisk footnote (P < 0.08) to the Hep G2 absolute IC50 values, so neither statistic belongs to the fibroblast column; P is therefore N/A / not_found_in_source rather than a recorded inequality. Effect detail: fibroblast IC50 means 8.5 +/- 5.6 (E4/4) vs 9.3 +/- 4.6 (E3/3) ug apoB/ml, paired ratio 0.94 +/- 0.49. n = 7 is the count of pairs with fibroblast VLDL entries in Table 2 (pair 6 has no fibroblast values); Methods say eight pairs overall. The fibroblast donor is a single healthy male foreskin line, so the receptor-bearing cell is one genotype-unspecified non-brain human cell while only the ligand varies by APOE genotype. Merged 2026-11-23: an earlier extraction filed the unpaired IC50 comparison as a separate against row; that double-counted one experiment. A one-sample test of a within-pair ratio against unity is not strictly a two-group E4-vs-E3 test.

description: LDL isolated from APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 donors competed equally against 125I-LDL for the LDL receptor on both Hep G2 cells and fibroblasts, giving no isoform difference in binding for the LDL particle in either cell type.
quote: In summary, those results showed that there was not a significant difference between the affinity of LDL particles from E4/4 and E3/3 subjects in either Hep G2 cells or fibroblasts.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LDL competition IC50 at the LDL receptor, both cell types)
system: Hep G2 human hepatoma cells and foreskin fibroblasts from a healthy male donor, grown to 75% confluence and preincubated 24-48 h in lipoprotein-deficient serum, incubated 2 h at 4 C and pH 7.4 with 10 ug apoB/ml 125I-LDL plus a concentration range of native LDL isolated by equilibrium density gradient ultracentrifugation from APOE4/4 or paired APOE3/3 male donors aged 42 +/- 6 and 45 +/- 7 years; competition IC50 in ug apoB/ml, paired E4/4-to-E3/3 ratio.
location: Table 4, fibroblast and Hep G2 columns
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Against: true, a null for the LDL particle. This row covers both cell types because the authors state the LDL result as one sentence spanning both and Table 4 carries no P value or footnote for either column; P is N/A / not_found_in_source. The brief asks for one condition per row, so the human may prefer this split into a fibroblast row (paired ratio 0.92 +/- 0.24, IC50 12.3 +/- 4.1 vs 13.6 +/- 2.1) and a Hep G2 row (paired ratio 0.93 +/- 0.37, IC50 14.0 +/- 5.4 vs 15.4 +/- 2.1); the eff recorded here is the Hep G2 ratio 0.93 and the fibroblast ratio is 0.92, so the two are within rounding of each other. n = 6 is the smaller of the two columns' pair counts in Table 4 (fibroblasts: pairs 1-4, 6, 7; Hep G2 has 7 pairs); recorded conservatively rather than picking the larger end. Table 5 adds a concordant null on VLDL-free plasma versus LDL (E4/4 vs E3/3 P = 0.20), which is not filed as a separate H4 row because it compares preparations rather than measuring an isoform binding difference.

description: In direct (non-competitive) binding studies on Hep G2 cells the dissociation constants for VLDL from APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 donors were the same, an isoform null that the authors report without a figure or table.
quote: Indeed, in direct binding studies on the VLDL of six E4/4 and six E3/3 subjects (not shown), we also did not find any difference in affinity between E4/4 and E3/3 subjects in binding to Hep G2 cells at 4°C (K d values: 22 ± 11 vs. 21 ± 10 nM, respectively).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in VLDL Kd for binding to Hep G2 cells)
system: Hep G2 human hepatoma cells at 4 C, direct saturation binding of 125I-labelled native VLDL isolated from six APOE4/4 and six APOE3/3 male donors aged 42 +/- 6 and 45 +/- 7 years, VLDL radioiodinated by the iodine monochloride method; dissociation constant Kd in nmol/l.
location: Discussion, data not shown (direct binding on Hep G2)
human_check: No figure image was viewed; this result has no figure or table at all, being reported as 'not shown' in the Discussion, so it cannot be checked against a panel and its location is a text location rather than a panel. Against: true, a direct-binding null that runs counter to the same paper's competition result on the same cell type; the authors attribute the discrepancy to iodination damage in direct binding, which is their interpretation and not a measurement. Kd 22 +/- 11 (E4/4) vs 21 +/- 10 (E3/3) nM; no P printed, hence N/A / not_found_in_source, and eff is qualitative because the authors print no percent or fold for this contrast. Direct binding of VLDL may also reflect binding to receptors other than the LDL receptor, which the authors say explicitly, so the receptor identity is less certain here than in the competition assays.
